scene: Ānanda tells the Buddha that good friendship seems to be half of the spiritual life. The Buddha corrects him and calls it the whole.
question: How much of the path depends on having good friends, companions, and examples?
main_point: Good friendship supplies the conditions in which the whole path can be developed. The Buddha then points to himself as the decisive example of a good friend: through relying on his teaching, people can practice toward freedom.
reading_cue: The long middle section names all eight parts of the path. You do not need to memorize them here. Follow the repeated point that good friendship supports the development of every part.
not_saying: The text is not saying that pleasant company by itself completes the path. Its idea of a good friend is someone whose example and guidance support the entire course of practice.
evidence_sections: The Buddha as a Good Friend
